tested_combination.sdk_pin_origin: pyproject.toml declares skillweave-sdk==0.1.0; the workflow resolves its tag from that pin, so the CI clone is v0.1.0. The newer v0.2.0 tag (0fb2907bef0c531493e0967f6eb34a430cce6905) carries byte-identical schemas and the same canonical digest d334d1f8, so the contract check is independent of the tag label.
tested_combination.canonical_digest_algorithm: sha256 of the sorted '<name>:<sha256>\n' concatenation of every SDK schemas/*.schema.json entry

evidence.meaning: The SDK at the Core contract pin (skillweave-sdk==0.1.0, tag v0.1.0) carries four schemas, not the nine lifecycle contracts; the eight fixture contracts have no SDK schema and the cross-repo suite fails.

AC5 local reproduction: the canonical-digest check passes on the pristine published SDK clone at the Core contract pin (tag v0.1.0, pytest exit 0) and fails once a single byte is appended to schemas/run-state.schema.json (pytest exit 1); the full suite against the drifted SDK is 3 failed, 12 passed (exit 1).

blocked_criteria.title: All nine SDK schemas and all Core fixtures validated; a missing SDK schema is a failure
blocked_criteria.reason: The published SDK at the current contract pin (skillweave-sdk==0.1.0, tag v0.1.0) declares only the four pre-lifecycle schemas. The eight Core lifecycle fixtures (work-profile, lifecycle-profile, deliverable-contract, evidence-contract, category-pack, category-taxonomy, model-provider, search-provider) have no SDK schema, so the requirement cannot be satisfied without first publishing the lifecycle schema set.
blocked_criteria.fail_closed_enforcement: Both positive validator tests now report a missing SDK schema as a failure: test_all_fixtures_validate_against_sdk_schemas (Core-side) and test_external_consumer_validates_fixtures_independently (external-consumer-side, whose silent `continue` was removed in SW-1591-CI-001). A missing schema can never be skipped.

blocked_criteria.title: Green real Forgejo workflow run with linked run evidence
blocked_criteria.reason: A real Forgejo run cannot be green: the cross-repo suite fails by design because the published SDK lacks eight lifecycle schemas. Contract CI is correctly fail-closed (not false-green): the pristine published SDK yields exactly two honest reds in tests/integration/test_cross_repo_contract_ci.py, both the same root cause (missing published lifecycle schemas).
